name: hydra-file-findings
description: Turn a reviewer's findings into forge issues — the flow port of orchestrate.sh's create_finding_issues (hydra-flows-first-port 6.1).
$comment: WHAT THIS REPLACES. `create_finding_issues()` in orchestrate.sh: read the reviewer's
JSON, take the open WARNING and SUGGESTION findings, and file one issue each. It was the
ONE function in that 3,258-line file the audit could not call superseded, and therefore
the reason the file could not be deleted.
WHY IT NEEDED FOUR CHANGES ELSEWHERE BEFORE IT COULD BE WRITTEN, each found only by
openregister#2246  the broker refused POST /repos/*/issues, so nothing could file one
hermiq#104         findings live in the clone, which is deleted — the stage now returns files
hermiq#105         they came back as TEXT; a flow cannot address into a string
openregister#2247  nothing turned a list ON an item INTO items; `explode` is that primitive
hermiq#106         `files['reviews/latest.json']` is unreachable by any dotted path — hence the alias
WHY THE FILTER IS A SEPARATE EDGE rather than a condition on the explode. The severity
and status rules are hydra's POLICY — only open WARNING and SUGGESTION findings become
issues, because an ERROR already failed the gate and a resolved finding is history. Policy
belongs where someone reading the canvas can see and change it, not buried in a node's
config. That is the whole argument for the port.
WHY ONE ISSUE PER FINDING and not one summary issue: the shell did it this way, and a
summary issue cannot be closed per-finding as each is fixed. Preserving the granularity is
what makes this a PORT rather than a redesign.

config.$comment: `stage.files.findings` is the reviewer JSON, collected under an ALIAS by the stage — the raw path `reviews/latest.json` cannot be walked, because the key holds dots and slashes. The item's own record is carried, so each finding still knows its repo and run.
hydra's POLICY, kept visible on the canvas: an ERROR already failed the gate, and a finding that is not open is history. Only open WARNING and SUGGESTION findings become issues.

body.title: [hydra] {{finding.title}}

config.$comment: One issue per finding. The body names the run and the ref so a reader can get back to what produced it — a finding with no provenance is a bug report nobody can act on. `onError: continue` deliberately: one finding that fails to file must not discard the rest, and the run's own trace records which.
